content: I have preserved the detailed nature of the content without summarizing it. 1. GA (Gas): A gas that is packaged in a pressurized bottle or tank for use. 2. GD (Gel for direct application): A gel-like preparation intended to be applied undiluted. 3. GE (Gas generating product): A formulation that produces gas through a chemical reaction. 4. GL (Emulsifiable gel): A gelatinized formulation designed to be applied as an emulsion in water. 5. GR (Granule): A free-flowing solid formulation with a defined granule size range, ready for use. 6. GS (Grease): A highly viscous formulation based on oil or fat. 7. GW (Water-soluble gel): A gelatinized formulation intended to be applied as an aqueous solution. 8. HN (Hot fogging concentrate): A formulation suitable for application using hot fogging equipment, either directly or after dilution. 9. KK (Combi-pack solid/liquid): A combination of a solid and a liquid formulation, separately contained within one outer pack, intended for simultaneous application in a tank mix. 10. KL (Combi-pack liquid/liquid): Two liquid formulations, separately contained within one outer pack, intended for simultaneous application in a tank mix. 11. KN (Cold fogging concentrate): A formulation suitable for application using cold fogging equipment, either directly or after dilution. 12. LN (Long-lasting insecticidal net): A slowor controlled-release formulation in the form of netting, providing both physical and chemical barriers to insects. This includes bulk netting and ready-to-use products, such as mosquito nets. 13. LB (Long-lasting storage bag): A slowor controlled-release formulation in the form of a treated bag for storage, offering physical and chemical barriers, for example, against pests. 14. LS (Solution for seed treatment): A clear to opalescent liquid applied to seeds either directly or as a solution of the active ingredient after dilution in water. The liquid may contain water-insoluble formulants. 15. MC (Mosquito coil): A coil that smolders without producing a flame, releasing the active ingredient into the local atmosphere as vapor or smoke. 16. ME (Micro-emulsion): A clear to opalescent liquid containing oil and water, applied directly or after dilution in water, forming either a diluted micro-emulsion or a conventional emulsion. 17. MR (Matrix release): A slowor controlled-release formulation in the form of a polymer matrix, providing long-lasting effects. It is intended for direct application. 18. OD (Oil dispersion): A stable suspension of active ingredients in a water-immiscible fluid, which may also contain dissolved active ingredients, intended for dilution with water before use. 19. OF (Oil miscible flowable concentrate): A stable suspension of active ingredients in a fluid, intended for dilution in an organic liquid before use. 20. OL (Oil miscible liquid): A homogeneous liquid formulation to be applied as a homogeneous liquid after dilution in an organic liquid. 21. OP (Oil dispersible powder): A powder formulation to be applied as a suspension after dispersion in an organic liquid. 22. PA (Paste): A water-based, film-forming composition. 23. PR (Plant rodlet): A small rodlet, typically a few centimeters in length and a few millimeters in diameter, containing an active ingredient. 24. RB (Bait, ready for use): A formulation designed to attract and be consumed by target pests. 25. SC (Suspension concentrate): A stable suspension of active ingredients in water, intended for dilution with water before use. 26. SD (Suspension concentrate for direct application): A stable suspension of active ingredients in a fluid, which may also contain dissolved active ingredients, intended for direct application, such as to rice paddies. 27. SE (Suspo-emulsion): A heterogeneous fluid formulation consisting of a stable dispersion of active ingredients in the form of solid particles and fine globules in a continuous water phase. 28. SG (Water-soluble granule): A formulation consisting of granules to be applied as a true solution of the active ingredient after dissolution in water, though it may contain insoluble inert ingredients. 29. SL (Soluble concentrate): A clear to opalescent liquid applied as a solution of the active ingredient after dilution in water. The liquid may contain water-insoluble formulants. 30. SO (Spreading oil): A formulation designed to form a surface layer upon application to water. 31. SP (Water-soluble powder): A powder formulation applied as a true solution of the active ingredient after dissolution in water, though it may contain insoluble inert ingredients. 32. ST (Water-soluble tablet): A tablet formulation used individually to form a solution of the active ingredient after disintegration in water. The formulation may contain water-insoluble formulants. 33. SU (Ultra-low volume suspension): A suspension ready for use through ultra-low volume (ULV) equipment. 34. TB (Tablet): Pre-formed solids of uniform shape and dimensions, usually circular, with either flat or convex faces, where the distance between faces is less than the diameter. 35. TC (Technical material): A material resulting from a manufacturing process, comprising the active ingredient along with associated impurities. It may contain small amounts of necessary additives. 36. TK (Technical concentrate): A material resulting from a manufacturing process, comprising the active ingredient along with associated impurities. It may also contain small amounts of necessary additives and appropriate diluents. 37. UL (Ultra-low volume liquid): A homogeneous liquid ready for use through ULV equipment. 38. VP (Vapor releasing product): A formulation containing one or more volatile active ingredients, the vapors of which are released into the air. The evaporation rate is typically controlled using suitable formulations and/or dispensers. 39. WG (Water-dispersible granules): A formulation consisting of granules to be applied after disintegration and dispersion in water. 40. WP (Wettable powder): A powder formulation applied as a suspension after dispersion in water. 41. WS (Water-dispersible powder for slurry seed treatment): A powder to be dispersed at high concentration in water before application as a slurry to seeds. 42. WT (Water-dispersible tablet): A tablet formulation used individually to form a dispersion of the active ingredient after disintegration in water. 43. XX (Others): A temporary categorization for all other formulations not listed above. 44. ZC (Mixed formulation of CS and SC): A stable suspension of capsules and active ingredients in fluid, typically intended for dilution with water before use. 45. ZE (Mixed formulation of CS and SE): A heterogeneous fluid formulation consisting of a stable dispersion of active ingredients in the form of capsules, solid particles, and fine globules in a continuous water phase, typically intended for dilution with water before use. 46. ZW (Mixed formulation of CS and EW): A heterogeneous fluid formulation consisting of a stable dispersion of active ingredients in the form of capsules and fine globules in a continuous water phase, typically intended for dilution with water before use.
